Class KittyKeyboardSupport

java.lang.Object
dev.tamboui.terminal.KittyKeyboardSupport
public final class KittyKeyboardSupport extends Object
Constants, escape-sequence builders and optional terminal-side detection for the Kitty keyboard protocol (progressive keyboard enhancements).

TamboUI pushes keyboard enhancement flags unconditionally on startup via Backend.enableKeyboardProtocol(KeyboardProtocol) and pops them on shutdown via Backend.disableKeyboardProtocol(). Terminals that do not implement the protocol ignore both sequences; terminals that do implement it preserve any flags set by a parent process (shell integration, wrapping TUI, tmux) via the protocol's wire-level stack.

Apps that need to detect whether the current terminal actually supports the protocol (for UI adaptation, feature gating, or diagnostics) can call query(Backend, int). This is opt-in and never invoked by the runner; the runner's default behaviour is push-unconditionally.

Escape sequences used:

  • Push flags: CSI > <flags> u
  • Pop flags: CSI < u
  • Query flags: CSI ? u
  • Query response: CSI ? <flags> u

    • query

      public static int query(Backend backend, int timeoutMs) throws IOException
      Queries the terminal for Kitty keyboard protocol support.

      Sends the CSI ? u query sequence and parses the CSI ? <flags> u response. Returns the reported flags bitmask on success, 0 if the terminal responded with no flags enabled, or -1 if the terminal did not respond within the timeout (treat as "protocol not supported" for feature detection).

      This method is opt-in: TamboUI's runner never calls it. Apps that want to detect support for UI adaptation or diagnostics can call it directly, typically before invoking Backend.enableKeyboardProtocol(KeyboardProtocol).

      Warning: query consumes bytes from the backend's input stream. Do not call it concurrently with other code reading input (such as the TuiRunner's input reader). Call it before starting the runner, or on a backend that is not yet attached to one.

      Parameters:
      backend - the terminal backend
      timeoutMs - timeout in milliseconds to wait for response
      Returns:
      the reported flags bitmask, or -1 if unsupported or timed out
      Throws:
      IOException - if an I/O error occurs
